newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco finds new nickel zone at Voisey's Bay.
newsitem.headline: Inco finds new nickel zone at Voisey's Bay.

text.p: Inco Ltd said on Friday it has found a new mineralized zone at its Voisey's Bay nickel, copper and cobalt deposit in remote Voisey's Bay, Labrador.
The new zone lies beneath and next to a shallow zone in the Western Extension, one of three main Voisey's Bay deposits previously announced.

Inco said it has 20 drillholes in the zone so far, showing the zone is about 250 to 600 metres below surface over a strike length of 500 metres. Assays in the core of the zone vary from 1.2 percent to 2.8 percent nickel, "significantly higher" than nickel content found in the Eastern Deeps.
Copper and cobalt in the assays are also higher to those found in the Eastern Deeps, Inco said.

In the eastern section of the zone, drilling has shown three separate intervals of mineralization grading 1.48 percent nickel over 36.8 percent metres, 2.5 percent over 9.5 metres and 2.8 percent over 14.3 metres, Inco said.
The area east of this drill section is open for at least 700 metres, Inco said.
The company said it will continue drilling in order to come up with a resource calcuation. Drilling continues in the Western Extension and Eastern Deeps as well, Inco said.
Shares in Inco spiked on the news, rising C$1.85 at one point to C$47.25 before settling at C$46.50, up C$1.10.
Shares in Voisey's Bay Nickel Co rose C$0.45 to C$32.20 on the news.
